title: Best AI phone answering solutions for car dealerships in 2026
summary: Compare our AI phone answering with Numa, Impel, Podium, Drivee and CallRail Voice Assist using official sources and practical workflow tests.
body_markdown:
The best AI phone answering for a car dealership is the product that handles the store’s actual call, completes a permitted next step and gives unresolved work to the right person. Voice quality matters, but so do appointment accuracy, routing, current information and the connected-system result.


Compare **our platform, Clearline, with Numa, Impel Voice AI, Podium Service AI, Drivee and CallRail Voice Assist** against that workflow. This shortlist is based on official public product material reviewed **October 26, 2026** , not independent performance testing. We publish this guide and include our platform in it. The[dealership AI buying hub](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/pillars/dealership-ai-buying-guide) explains the wider selection process.


## Match the product to the phone problem


Product Published scope Put it on the shortlist when Verify live


[Clearline (our platform)](https://www.useclearline.com/product/inbound) Inbound conversations, configured booking/actions, campaigns and native CRM records You want calls connected to opportunities, tasks and follow-up across departments Permitted actions, staff ownership and exact system writes


[Numa](https://numa.com/) Automotive voice, service appointments, shared inbox, call intelligence and sales products Service-call handling and connected customer context are central requirements Your DMS/scheduler, booking rules and unresolved-work path


[Impel Voice AI](https://impel.ai/voice-ai/) Service-call assistant, booking, routing, voicemail coverage and SMS follow-up You need service voice and recovery alongside a wider automotive AI package Live versus voicemail path, dropped booking and advisor worklist


[Podium Service AI](https://automotive.podium.com/solutions/service) Service voice, DMS scheduling, contextual transfers and outreach Your evaluation includes service conversations and proactive customer outreach Calendar/DMS actions, routing and selected package scope


[Drivee](https://drivee.ai/ai-voice-agent/) Automotive inbound/outbound voice, qualification, inventory-aware conversation and booking Sales calls should use approved inventory context Feed freshness, sold vehicles, price boundaries and booking result


[CallRail Voice Assist](https://www.voiceassist.callrail.com/) Calls/texts, intake, qualification, scheduling, routing and follow-up You want to evaluate general business AI answering with CallRail’s broader tools Automotive inventory, DMS, OP-code and department-specific requirements


This is a fit-based shortlist, not a universal ranking. Capabilities on a website may require a specific plan, integration or configuration. Have each vendor show the actual product proposed for your store.


## Our approach: calls connected to customer work


Our[inbound product](https://www.useclearline.com/product/inbound) supports customer conversations alongside[campaigns](https://www.useclearline.com/product/campaigns) ,[scheduling](https://www.useclearline.com/product/scheduler) and a native[CRM](https://www.useclearline.com/product/crm) . Our customer records connect contacts with related vehicles, opportunities, tasks, meetings and conversation history.


We let you enable booking, cancellation, rescheduling and inventory search separately. Booking requires selected calendars; repair-order status depends on available PBS data.


Ask to see a call become a usable customer record and next action. Distinguish configured automatic work from tasks a staff member completes. Native CRM scope is an additional buying consideration; it does not make every DMS write available automatically.


## Numa: automotive call and service context


Numa publishes service voice, appointment, inbox and opportunity workflows alongside call intelligence, routing and sales products. Its website names DMS and scheduling connections and describes a dealership-specific customer context.


Ask for your exact systems and rooftops. Test an appointment, an advisor request and a question that requires data the connection cannot provide. Confirm whether the AI completes the action or leaves work for staff.


## Impel Voice AI: live service calls and recovery


Impel’s Voice AI page describes a live Digital Voice Assistant, appointment booking, routing, voicemail coverage and SMS follow-up. It also describes continuing a dropped booking over text and an advisor worklist.


Those exception paths deserve a test. Ask what happens when an advisor cannot answer, the caller disconnects or the requested service falls outside the approved booking rules. Confirm which broader Impel products are included in the quote.


## Podium Service AI: voice and service outreach


Podium’s Service AI page describes inbound calls, DMS appointment scheduling, contextual transfers and proactive outreach using connected service data.


Ask to see the actual customer, appointment and staff handoff records. Check how the selected package uses data, how replies change outreach and which requirements stay in another CRM or service tool.


## Drivee: inventory-aware sales voice


Drivee’s automotive voice page presents inbound/outbound calling, buyer qualification, inventory context and booking. The useful test is whether the conversation uses current approved information and stays within the dealership’s commitments.


Ask about a sold unit, change a vehicle requirement and request a payment quote. Verify the feed, available alternatives and human escalation. Demonstrate where an accepted visit is actually booked.


## CallRail Voice Assist: answering as well as attribution


CallRail’s[Voice Assist](https://www.callrail.com/voice-assist) supports answering calls and texts, collecting information, scheduling and routing. Evaluate those actions and their configuration rather than treating the product only as after-call analytics.


The reviewed general business material does not establish dealership DMS writes, automotive inventory freshness or OP-code booking rules. Put those requirements in the test if they matter to your store. A general appointment integration may be useful without completing every dealership-specific service workflow.


## Seven calls to test with every vendor


Use test records and the same scenarios:


1. **After-hours sales inquiry:** ask about a specific vehicle, then change a requirement. Verify current information and a usable next step.
2. **Service booking:** request a service, reject the first time and inspect the appointment record.
3. **Repair-order status:** ask a question requiring connected data. The system must use approved information or route it appropriately.
4. **Human request:** ask for an employee and repeat the test when that employee cannot answer. Show the fallback owner.
5. **Correction or interruption:** change the customer’s details and confirm the next response uses the correction.
6. **Unsupported commitment:** request a financing approval, final price or diagnosis. Confirm the human boundary.
7. **Incomplete booking:** leave before confirming, then reply later. Show what staff see and how follow-up continues under the store’s rules.


Record accuracy, successful appointment actions, transfer results, unresolved tasks and connected-system behavior. The[vendor evaluation scorecard](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-dealership-ai-vendors) provides a fuller acceptance sheet.


## Check phone coverage and system fit separately


Routing determines which calls reach the AI: main line, department line, overflow, direct-dial employee numbers or after hours. Test the actual phone paths and failed transfers, not just the vendor’s demo number.


Then map data and actions. For example, our[PBS integration](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/clearline-pbs-systems-integration) distinguishes supported two-way contacts, vehicles and service appointments from pull-only Workplan events, tasks/reminders and appointments. Require equivalent clarity for every proposed connection.


If you also need a place for staff to manage opportunities, compare[automotive CRM software](https://www.useclearline.com/blog/best-automotive-crm-software) . If the existing CRM remains, define which product owns records and outreach to prevent duplicate work.


## Measure the pilot against the operating gap


Baseline answered calls, missed/abandoned calls, meaningful response time, correct bookings, successful transfers, unresolved requests and appointment attendance by department and daypart.


Review failures and customer outcomes as well as activity. A larger answered-call count does not prove a sale or repair order was incremental. Avoid adopting vendor outcome percentages as a forecast for your own dealership.


To evaluate our platform,[bring one sales call and one service request to a demo](https://www.useclearline.com/demo) . Follow the conversation, staff work and resulting records before comparing the quote.


## Frequently asked questions


What is the best AI phone answering solution for a dealership? +


The right fit depends on the call paths, booking rules, data and staff workflow. Compare the current shortlist using the same calls and inspect the resulting actions, not just the voice.


Does CallRail offer AI answering? +


Yes. Its current Voice Assist product answers calls/texts and supports intake, scheduling, routing and follow-up. Dealership-specific DMS and inventory requirements still need verification.


Is every voice AI product also a CRM? +


No. Some provide communication workflows around another customer system. Others include a native workspace. Ask to see customer records, opportunity stages, tasks and staff ownership separately.


Can AI book service appointments directly? +


Some configured products can. Demonstrate a successful booking, reschedule and cancellation on the dealership’s supported calendar or DMS, and inspect the record each time.
